notes: Distinguishes withdrawal-specific pause and ready queued withdrawal, but P omits general contract not paused.
I correctly prohibits withdrawal completion while withdrawal-specific pause is active.
Core claimed capability is downgraded to potential based on absence of an observed incident; emergencies/drains remain appropriately potential.
Report explicitly names redeem and withdraw, but model says withdraw being affected is unstated.
P preserves non-owner and self allowance but omits insufficient caller authorization, positive shares and receiver binding.
I requires caller allowance on every attempted non-owner call, rather than guarding successful spending; a correctly rejected unauthorized call can violate this I.
Burn and transfer are represented, including a combined claim, but unauthorized condition/attacker-controlled receiver remain incomplete.
All impacts downgraded to potential despite report asserting conditional theft capability.
I exactly states callback amount equals actual transferred amount.
P retains later claim and reliance, but cumulative entitlement versus transferred divergence is not explicitly constrained and claim history identity is unresolved.
V encodes mismatch but not callback amount equals cumulative entitlement as in the preliminary reference; cumulative-vs-transferred divergence is conflated with passed-vs-transferred mismatch.
Direct incorrect-value capability is downgraded to potential; downstream losses appropriately remain unformalized potential.
Symbol transferred_toSend also violates current snake_case symbol validation, independently of the first missing-path rejection.
Primary I has correct cooldown direction, but timestamp + seconds is rejected by the current strict same-unit arithmetic frontend; not counted as fully compatible formal I.
P is an implication from successful withdrawal to an implementation guard, not the intended deposit/positive cooldown/early withdrawal conditions.
Deposit/withdraw ordering and positive lock period are not formalized; lack of maturity write is preserved only in explanatory elements.
Secondary I forbids any rewards captured before maturity, which is stronger than prohibiting short-cycle liquidity exit and is insufficiently supported.
Primary capability and all broader impacts downgraded to potential; economic limits are documented.
Misses the relevant inferred obligation that valid nonzero trades must not be rejected as zero-cost.
I text says blocked only when zero-cost, but AST is zero_cost_trade => trade_blocked, the opposite implication of that only-when statement.
The stated I is satisfied by the false-positive revert and does not witness the claimed vulnerability.
Nonzero and bitwise-zero predicates are undeclared Boolean relations without numeric definitions; unsupported bitwise limitation is explicitly retained.
Core false-positive revert is asserted, repeated DoS remains potential/partial, and no fund-loss conclusion is invented.
